ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left of the figure is an AC power supply labeled 400 V, 50 Hz, connected to the left 400 V winding of a three-winding transformer. There are also two 200 V windings in the figure, labeled 400:200:200. The upper end of the right 200 V winding is connected to the upper end of the voltmeter, and the lower end of the voltmeter is connected back to the lower end of the left power supply through the bottom wire; the upper end of the middle 200 V winding is connected to the upper end of the power supply, and the lower end of the middle winding is connected to the lower end of the right 200 V winding. Reasoning: According to the specified method, take the node where the lower end of the power supply and the lower end of the voltmeter are located as 0 V, and the upper end of the power supply as +400 V. The upper end of the middle 200 V winding is connected to the +400 V node; according to the winding polarity in the figure, its lower-end potential is +400 V - 200 V = +200 V. The right 200 V winding is connected from this common lower end to the upper end of the voltmeter, and the polarity is opposite, so from the common lower end to the upper end of the voltmeter the potential changes another 200 V toward the lower end of the power supply, that is, the upper end of the voltmeter is +200 V - 200 V = 0 V. Both the upper and lower ends of the voltmeter are 0 V, so the reading is 0 V.

method.method_draft: Take the lower source/voltmeter node as 0 V and the upper source node as +400 V. Since the middle winding is rated 200 V and its upper terminal is connected to the +400 V node, use the polarity shown by the winding sense to place its lower terminal at +200 V. The right-hand 200 V winding is connected from that common lower terminal to the voltmeter upper terminal with opposite polarity, so moving to the voltmeter upper terminal changes the potential by another 200 V toward the lower source node, giving 0 V. The voltmeter is therefore between two equipotential points, so it reads 0 V.

planner_metadata.knowledge_role: For an ideal transformer, induced voltages are proportional to turns ratings and have polarities determined by winding sense/dot convention. Equal 200 V windings on the same core produce equal magnitudes; when connected with opposing polarity, their voltage contributions cancel or can step a node potential down by 200 V each according to the chosen direction.

method.method_draft: Identify the loop from the 400 V source upper terminal through the two 200 V windings to the voltmeter and back to the source lower terminal. From the 400:200:200 rating, each of the two right-hand windings has 200 V induced. From the drawn winding orientation and their connection, these two induced voltages are series-aiding in the sense that their total 400 V opposes the applied 400 V source in that loop. Use KVL: voltmeter voltage = applied source voltage − induced series voltage = 400 − (200 + 200) = 0 V.
